source: When the publication updated the list in 2012 to include the first decade of the new millennium, not only did the Beatles’ classic remain at #1 but the entire top 10 was unchanged.
claim: The 2003 and 2012 top 10s contain the same ten albums in the same order, with Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band #1 in both.
code: a[a['2003 Rank'].le(10) | a['2012 Rank'].le(10)].assign(same_rank=lambda d: d['2003 Rank'].eq(d['2012 Rank']))[['Album', '2003 Rank', '2012 Rank', 'same_rank']].sort_values('2003 Rank')

source: Beyond “What’s Going On” jumping from #6 to #1 and “Pet Sounds” remaining locked in at #2, the entire top 10 was changed, some albums jumping scores of spots.
claim: Only two albums in the 2020 top 10—What's Going On, up from #6 to #1, and Pet Sounds, still #2—were also in the 2003 top 10.
code: a[a['2020 Rank'].le(10)].assign(in_2003_top10=lambda d: d['2003 Rank'].le(10))[['Album', '2003 Rank', '2020 Rank', 'in_2003_top10']].sort_values('2020 Rank')

source: Here is the complete ranking from 2020, and nearly a third of the albums were new, never appearing in previous rankings.
claim: 154 of the 500 albums in the 2020 ranking (30.8%) had not appeared in either the 2003 or the 2012 ranking.
code: a[a['2020 Rank'].notna()].assign(new=lambda d: d['2003 Rank'].isna() & d['2012 Rank'].isna())['new'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean'])

source: Here are the 174 albums from the 2003 ranking that failed to rank twenty years later.
claim: 174 of the 500 albums in the 2003 ranking (34.8%) are absent from the 2020 ranking.

source: 18% are compilations or greatest hits albums.
claim: 31 of the 174 albums that dropped out (17.8%) are compilations or greatest hits albums.
code: a.loc[a['2003 Rank'].notna() & a['2020 Rank'].isna(), 'Album Type'].isin(['Compilation', 'Greatest Hits']).agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean'])

source: Here we add in albums unavailable on Spotify that still made Rolling Stone’s 2020 list. About half of these albums (in red) saw their ranking decline.
claim: Of the 22 albums not on Spotify that made the 2020 list, 10 (45.5%) had a worse 2020 rank than 2003 rank.
code: a[(a['Spotify URI'] == 'Not on Spotify') & a['2020 Rank'].notna()].assign(declined=lambda d: d['2020 Rank'] > d['2003 Rank'])['declined'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean'])

source:
Billboard #1 Album: 30% of albums
Top 100 Albums in the 2020 Ranking
Billboard #2-100: 60%
#101+: 4%
Never charted: 6%
claim: Among the 100 albums in the 2020 top 100, 30% peaked at Billboard #1, 60% between #2 and #100, 4% between #101 and #200, and 6% never charted.

source: If we look at Rolling Stone’s lower ranked albums, meaning those among the bottom 400, they are 3x more likely to have never charted on Billboard.
claim: 72 of the 400 albums in the 2020 bottom 400 (18%) never charted on Billboard, against 6 of the 100 top-100 albums (6%), three times the rate.
code: a[a['2020 Rank'].notna()].assign(never=lambda d: d['Peak Billboard Position'].eq(201), group=lambda d: np.where(d['2020 Rank'].le(100), 'top100', 'bottom400')).groupby('group')['never'].agg(['sum', 'count', 'mean']).assign(ratio=lambda d: d.loc['bottom400', 'mean'] / d.loc['top100', 'mean'])

claim: 242 of the 269 voters in 2003 (90%) were men.

source: Not surprisingly, voters selected predominantly male performers—nearly 82% of the 500 albums selected were by men.
claim: 410 of the 500 albums in the 2003 ranking (82%) are by male artists.

source: For the 2020 ranking, Rolling Stone – perhaps in an effort to poll beyond the musical tastes of white men – expanded the voting group from 269 to 336 and doubled the representation of women voters.
claim: Women voters rose from 26 of 269 voters in 2003 (9.7%) to 73 of 336 in 2020 (21.7%).

source: In 2020, over half of the judges were teenagers in the 1990s, 2000s, and 2010s.
claim: 191 of the 336 judges in 2020 (56.8%) were teenagers in the 1990s, 2000s or 2010s.

source: In 2003, for example, only 11 voters (4%) were teens in the 1990s. ... In 2020, the number of voters who grew up in the 1990s jumped from 11 (4%) to 90 (25%).
claim: The number of voters who were teenagers in the 1990s rose from 11 of 269 (4.1%) in 2003 to 90 of 336 in 2020.

Of the 104 albums from the 1990s on the 2020 list, 55 (53%) were on the list in 2003.

Of the 73 albums from the 1980s on the 2020 list, 56 (76%) were on the list in 2003.
’70s Albums
Of the 155 albums from the 1970s on the 2020 list, 128 (83%) were on the list in 2003.
’60s Albums
Of the 71 albums from the 1960s on 2020 list, 65 (92%) were on the list in 2003.
’50s Albums
Of the 10 albums from the 1950s on the 2020 list, 8 (80%) were on the in 2003.
claim: By release decade, 55 of 104 albums from the 1990s (52.9%), 56 of 73 from the 1980s (76.7%), 128 of 155 from the 1970s (82.6%), 65 of 71 from the 1960s (91.5%) and 8 of 10 from the 1950s (80%) on the 2020 list were also on the 2003 list.
code: a[a['2020 Rank'].notna()].assign(decade=lambda d: d['Release Year'] // 10 * 10).query('1950 <= decade <= 1990').groupby('decade').agg(n=('Album', 'size'), on_2003=('2003 Rank', lambda s: s.notna().sum())).assign(share=lambda d: d['on_2003'] / d['n'] * 100)
